sent_to_model:
Okay, I need help with a post for my blog. It's the little one only friends and a few ex-colleagues read, so no need to be careful about tone, but I do want it to be good. Short version: a parent complained about my busing oral history project, my principal wants me to quietly drop it, and I'm not going to. Jess texted me last night basically saying "it's one assignment, don't torch your job over it," and half the group chat agreed with her. I'd rather explain myself once, properly, than argue in fifteen texts. So it's sort of a post to all of them but really to Jess. I'm not mad at her, I get why she said it, and I don't want it to read like a lecture. Here's what I've got:

- juniors, US History II, 2 sections. project = interview someone in your family or neighborhood about Boston 1974-76 busing/desegregation, 10 min recording + 2 page reflection
- been doing it 4 years at Cobb Street High, never a complaint before
- complaint was an email to the principal (Dr. Halvorsen) + cc'd a school committee member. said the project 'reopens wounds' and 'pressures kids to judge their grandparents'
- meeting with Halvorsen and the parent is Thursday Nov 19, 3:15
- my plan: keep it, add an alternate option (interview a librarian/archivist or use the recorded interviews from past years, w/ permission) so no kid HAS to interview family
- 2023 a kid (D.) interviewed his grandmother who drove a school bus in Southie in '74. she'd never told anyone in the family. he played 40 sec of it for the class and nobody said a word for like a minute
- one girl last year found out her uncle threw rocks at a bus. she was upset. we talked after class twice. her reflection was the best thing I read all year
- Jess and I met student teaching at the same school 2012. she left teaching in 2019, now does HR at a biotech in Cambridge
- Jess isn't wrong that I could get burned. I'm untenured? no, tenured since 2021, but Halvorsen still controls my schedule and who gets AP
- the kids who are uncomfortable are the ones who need it most, but I don't get to force anyone. that's the line
- this is literally the history of the city they live in. the textbook gives it one paragraph
- honestly scared, a little. not brave about it
- Jess to understand why, not to agree necessarily
- make clear I'm not picking a fight with the parent, I actually think she has a point about pressure
- end on something warm, maybe that I'll text her Thursday after the meeting

(About me: high-school history teacher, 37, Boston, Massachusetts. Length: it should come to roughly 800-2,000 words.)

must_cover: Explains to Jess why the busing oral history project matters and will be retained, seeking understanding without requiring agreement.
Acknowledges the parent’s pressure concern, explains alternative interview options, and makes clear the teacher is not seeking confrontation with the parent.
Acknowledges the professional risks and Jess’s concern.

reference.kind: a model-written solution, used only to show the checks can be met
